# Elements in a small yard do not display what they should

### What happens
`recording.mp4` (0:32) shows a small yard: two floating elements hang side by side, and a penguin
walks a loop in front of them, carrying a smaller floating element above its head. Seen from the
front, all three floating elements display the same thing. From about 0:15 the camera walks around
the left floating element and then looks at the yard from behind. At several moments of the clip,
the floating elements and the penguin do not display what they should. These are separate,
independent defects, each affecting a different case; fixing one does not fix the others. The
terrain, the hills and the sky are drawn correctly.

### Expected
Each of these elements displays exactly what it was set up to display, at every moment and from
every side it is seen from. This must hold for any such element anywhere in the world and however it
is placed, turned or carried, not only for the elements and camera positions shown in the video.

### Environment
All.

- `/app/.harbor_assets/recording.mp4`

does not prescribe source files, internal names, or an implementation strategy.

language = "C++"
framework = "Luanti (Minetest)"
cross_file = true
visual_essentiality = "required"
difficulty = "hard"

difficulty_explanation = """
The text only says that the floating elements and the penguin in the yard do not display what they should at several moments, that the three floating elements display the same thing from the front, and that every such element must display what it was set up to display at every moment, from every side, however it is placed, turned or carried. It does not say that they are flat pictures, sprites or animations, and it names no defect, no object property and no code path. The video is the only place the five independent defects can be seen, all of them in the client's sprite-entity rendering (the "sprite" and "upright_sprite" visuals), spread over three source files plus the bundled Irrlicht engine. None of them logs anything, leaves a compiler warning, or breaks an existing unit test; the entity state the server and Lua see is correct in every case, so only the rendered pixels show them:

1. Left board frozen on "A" (the original issue #15105, src/client/content_cao.cpp + mesh.cpp/.h): the upright_sprite's frame is applied by rewriting the texture coordinates of a mesh whose vertices live in a static GPU buffer, and the buffer is never marked dirty, so the GPU keeps the first frame forever. The camera-facing board next to it (a billboard drawn from client memory) animates.
2. Camera-facing sprites mirrored (irr/src/CBillboardSceneNode.cpp, constructor): the billboard's corner texture coordinates are assigned with U flipped, so every "sprite" entity is drawn mirrored. In the video the right board's B, C and D read backwards and the penguin's side views point the wrong way, so it moonwalks when it crosses the yard. The defect sits in the engine library, not in Luanti's own sprite code, which looks correct.
3. Back of upright boards mirrored (src/client/content_cao.cpp, GenericCAO::addToScene): the back quad of an upright_sprite reuses the front quad's corners with the winding reversed, which reads naturally but maps the texture mirrored when seen from behind. From 0:23 the left board's back shows a mirrored "E" (its back sheet is E-F-G-K). The front is unaffected.
4. Penguin shows the wrong side (src/client/content_cao.cpp, GenericCAO::updateTexturePos): select_x_by_camera adds the entity's yaw to the camera bearing instead of subtracting it. Subjects turned along the view axis are unaffected; turned across it, front and back swap (seen along Z) or left and right swap (seen along X). In the video the penguin shows its back while walking towards the camera and its face while walking away.
5. Carried board frozen on "A" (src/client/content_cao.cpp, GenericCAO::step): the sprite frame timer was moved into the "not attached" branch of the movement code, so a sprite attached to another object never advances its animation. The board above the penguin's head stays on "A" while the two big boards cycle. It is a billboard, so fixing defect 1 does not touch it.

Several defects interact in the video (the penguin's moonwalk comes from defect 2, its back/face swap from defect 4, and the frozen carried board looks like defect 1 but has a different cause), so a fix guided only by one symptom is easy to get wrong: swapping the left/right or front/back columns of select_x_by_camera makes the penguin look right in this camera direction but fails the probes seen along the other axis, and flipping only the board that looks wrong leaves the other sprite paths broken.

The hidden tests run the real client headlessly (Xvfb, Mesa llvmpipe) on the devtest game with a probe world mod and classify the dominant colour of fixed screen regions over time (the whole scenario is run a second time if the harness itself fails, e.g. a client crash). Animated probes (an upright_sprite, an attached sprite, an attached upright_sprite, and an upright_sprite whose frame the mod changes with set_sprite() every second) must keep cycling through the sheet's frames in order at about one frame per second, and the animated ones must show the same frame as an identical unattached camera-facing sprite started at the same moment most of the time. A camera-facing sprite and the back of an upright_sprite with a four-quadrant texture must show each texture corner in the matching screen corner (catches mirrored and upside-down fixes). Four select_x_by_camera sprites turned to 0/90/180/270 degrees, seen once along -Z and once along +X, must each show the documented column for the side facing the camera. f2p per defect: 1 -> upright_sprite_animates, upright_sprite_follows_set_sprite, attached_upright_sprite_animates; 2 -> sprite_texture_is_not_mirrored; 3 -> upright_sprite_back_is_not_mirrored; 4 -> camera_facing_sprite_shows_the_side_facing_the_camera; 5 -> attached_sprite_animates, attached_upright_sprite_animates. The p2p tests (unattached camera-facing sprite animates in order and at the right rate, both quads render a palette colour, the front of an upright_sprite is not mirrored) reject fixes that flip every quad or double the frame rate. Non-oracle fixes (a non-buffered mesh instead of a dirty flag, a separate UV order for the back quad, a mirrored texture matrix instead of editing the billboard, a vector-based facing angle, a frame timer outside the movement branch) pass all tests; compensating fixes (swapped select_x columns, an upside-down billboard, a second frame timer) fail.
"""

I found and fixed four separate bugs, one for each wrong case in the video. The build compiles cleanly. I didn't re-render the scene, so the fixes haven't been checked visually; each one is based on the frames I pulled from the clip and on reading the code.

**1. Sprite images are drawn mirrored left-to-right** (`irr/src/CBillboardSceneNode.cpp`)
The right-hand element cycles A→B→C→D, and B, C and D come out reversed (A looks fine only because it's symmetric). The penguin's side views were reversed too, so its beak pointed backwards as it walked. The texture coordinates on the left and right edges of the camera-facing square were swapped. I put them back, which fixes every element of this type.

**2. The penguin picks the wrong view for the camera direction** (`src/client/content_cao.cpp`, `updateTexturePos`)
The penguin is a sprite sheet that shows a front, side or back view depending on where the camera is. The code added the penguin's facing angle when it should have subtracted it, so the penguin showed its back while walking toward the camera, and its front while walking away. Along with bug 1, this explains every wrong penguin view in the clip.

**3. Two-sided flat elements show their back image mirrored** (`src/client/content_cao.cpp`, `addToScene`)
Seen from behind, the left element showed a reversed "Ǝ" instead of "E". The back face reused the front face's corner layout with only the drawing order flipped, which mirrors the image. The back face now has its own layout, so its image reads correctly from behind.

**4. Carried elements never animate** (`src/client/content_cao.cpp`, `step`)
The element above the penguin's head stayed on "A" when it should have cycled frames like the right-hand one. The code that advances animation frames was inside the branch that only runs for objects that aren't attached to something. I moved it out so it runs for every object.

One gap: if a camera-dependent sprite like the penguin is itself carried, its view is still chosen from its angle relative to its carrier, not its angle in the world. That doesn't happen in this clip, and I left it as it was.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Turn the JUnit report into the task reward.

The reward is binary: 1.0 only when every configured f2p and p2p test is found exactly once in the
report and passed; otherwise 0.0. f2p_passed / f2p_total and p2p_passed / p2p_total record how close
a run came. The verifier reads test outcomes only, never the candidate's source.
"""
import html
import json
import argparse
import os
import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET

CONF = json.load(open("/tests/config.json"))
F2P, P2P = CONF["f2p"], CONF["p2p"]
REPORT = os.environ.get("JUNIT_OUT", "/logs/verifier/junit.xml")
OUT_DIR = "/logs/verifier"


def load_junit(path):
    """Every reported test, keyed by "classname name" and by name; a key seen twice with different
    outcomes counts as failed."""
    results = {}
    if not os.path.exists(path):
        return results
    try:
        root = ET.parse(path).getroot()
    except ET.ParseError:
        return results
    for tc in root.iter("testcase"):
        tags = {c.tag for c in tc}
        outcome = "skip" if "skipped" in tags else ("fail" if tags & {"failure", "error"} else "pass")
        full = f"{tc.get('classname', '')} {tc.get('name', '')}".strip()
        for key in {full, tc.get("name", "")}:
            if key in results and results[key] != outcome:
                results[key] = "fail"
            else:
                results[key] = outcome
    return results


def junit_key(test_id):
    """A pytest node id (tests/test_x.py::TestA::test_b[png]) as the JUnit report names it
    ("tests.test_x.TestA test_b[png]"); other ids unchanged."""
    if "::" not in test_id:
        return test_id
    parts = test_id.split("::")
    mod = parts[0][:-3] if parts[0].endswith(".py") else parts[0]
    return f"{'.'.join([mod.replace('/', '.')] + parts[1:-1])} {parts[-1]}"


def resolve(test_id, results):
    """The outcome of one configured test: an exact key match first (the id as written, or a
    pytest node id in JUnit form), else the single reported test whose key ends with it. Missing
    or ambiguous counts as not passed."""
    keys = [test_id, junit_key(test_id)]
    if " :: " in test_id:  # "file :: describe › test" (playwright list output)
        keys.append(test_id.replace(" :: ", " ", 1))
    if " > " in test_id:  # "describe > test": jest-junit joins with a space, playwright with " › "
        head, rest = test_id.split(" > ", 1)

# Capture the agent's submission BEFORE anything below mutates /app -- this is the last
# moment the tree is base + agent work; the restore loop and test.patch come next.
#
# A THROWAWAY INDEX, never /app/.git/index: `git add` against the real one would leave paths
# staged and change how the `git checkout harbor_base --` and `git clean` below behave.
#
# TRACKED EDITS + A SOURCE WHITELIST, not `add -A` with a blacklist. This image builds wx
# in-tree AFTER the harbor_base commit (environment/Dockerfile), so everything the build
# emits is untracked and NOT in wx's .gitignore. A bare `add -A` captured 380MB of .o/.d/.so;
# excluding those by extension still left ~120 configure-generated files (samples/*/Makefile,
# bk-deps, version-script, lib/wx/config/*, the utils/wxrc/wxrc binary) because most have no
# extension to blacklist. Inverting it -- stage tracked modifications, then add only untracked
# files that LOOK like source -- keeps the agent's work and drops generated output by default.
_SUB=/logs/verifier/submission.patch
_SUBIDX=/tmp/.submission_index
_SUBSRC=('*.c' '*.cc' '*.cpp' '*.cxx' '*.h' '*.hh' '*.hpp' '*.hxx' '*.inl' '*.m' '*.mm'
         '*.py' '*.rb' '*.go' '*.rs' '*.java' '*.js' '*.ts' '*.tsx' '*.cs' '*.kt' '*.swift')
rm -f "$_SUBIDX"
GIT_INDEX_FILE="$_SUBIDX" git -C /app read-tree harbor_base 2>>"$STDERR_LOG" || true
GIT_INDEX_FILE="$_SUBIDX" git -C /app add -u 2>>"$STDERR_LOG" || true
# Enumerate before adding: `git add` aborts and stages NOTHING if any one pathspec matches
# no file, which silently drops the agent's new files on most tasks.
# Generated-output dirs are dropped from the UNTRACKED scan only. A project that keeps real
# source under lib/ is unaffected: those files are tracked at harbor_base, so `add -u` above

mapfile -t _SUBNEW < <(git -C /app ls-files --others --exclude-standard \
  -- "${_SUBSRC[@]}" ':(exclude)lib/' ':(exclude)build/' ':(exclude).deps/' 2>/dev/null)
if [ "${#_SUBNEW[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then
  GIT_INDEX_FILE="$_SUBIDX" git -C /app add -- "${_SUBNEW[@]}" 2>>"$STDERR_LOG" || true
fi
GIT_INDEX_FILE="$_SUBIDX" git -C /app diff --binary --cached harbor_base \
  > "$_SUB" 2>>"$STDERR_LOG" || true
rm -f "$_SUBIDX"

# every change to a TRACKED file (any extension, deletions included) but only NEW files that
# look like source -- so an agent adding config.yml, a .cmake module or an extensionless script
# loses it, and the patch still looks clean. That is the failure this manifest exists to expose.
#
# NEWEST FIRST, which is the useful ordering and not a cosmetic one: build output and image
# assets are created before the agent phase starts, so anything the agent made sorts to the top.
# Build artifacts are excluded by the same rules as the capture, to keep the list readable.
#

_SUBCAP=/tmp/.submission_captured
if [ "${#_SUBNEW[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then printf '%s\n' "${_SUBNEW[@]}" > "$_SUBCAP"; else : > "$_SUBCAP"; fi

    ':(exclude)lib/' ':(exclude)build/' ':(exclude).deps/' \
    ':(exclude)*.o' ':(exclude)*.d' ':(exclude)*.a' ':(exclude)*.lo' ':(exclude)*.la' \
    ':(exclude)*.so' ':(exclude)*.so.*' ':(exclude)*.gch' ':(exclude)*.pyc' 2>/dev/null \
  | grep -vxF -f "$_SUBCAP" 2>/dev/null | wc -l)
{ echo "# Untracked files NOT captured into submission.patch, newest first."
  echo "# Anything the agent created sorts above build output, which predates the agent phase."
  echo "# total: ${_SUBSKIPN}  (showing at most 40)"
  git -C /app ls-files --others --exclude-standard -- . \
      ':(exclude)lib/' ':(exclude)build/' ':(exclude).deps/' \
      ':(exclude)*.o' ':(exclude)*.d' ':(exclude)*.a' ':(exclude)*.lo' ':(exclude)*.la' \
      ':(exclude)*.so' ':(exclude)*.so.*' ':(exclude)*.gch' ':(exclude)*.pyc' 2>/dev/null \
    | grep -vxF -f "$_SUBCAP" 2>/dev/null | head -200 \
    | while IFS= read -r _f; do
        printf '%s\t%s\t%s\n' "$(stat -c %Y "/app/$_f" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)" \
                              "$(stat -c %s "/app/$_f" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)" "$_f"
      done \
    | sort -rn | head -40 | awk -F'\t' '{printf "%s\t%s\t%s\n",$1,$2,$3}'

rm -f "$_SUBCAP"

# Size guard. The whitelist is a heuristic, so a task laying out source unusually could still
# produce something enormous. Cap it and leave a diagnosable stub: a truncated capture is
# recoverable, a full disk is not.
_SUBSZ=$(wc -c < "$_SUB" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)

  { echo "SUBMISSION CAPTURE SUPPRESSED: ${_SUBSZ} bytes exceeds the 5MB cap."
    echo "Directories contributing to the discarded patch:"
    grep -a "^diff --git" "$_SUB" | sed 's#^diff --git a/##; s# b/.*##; s#/[^/]*$##' \
      | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head -20
  } > "$_SUB.suppressed" 2>/dev/null
  : > "$_SUB"
  echo "== submission.patch SUPPRESSED (${_SUBSZ} bytes > 5MB cap) ==" | tee -a "$STDOUT_LOG"
else
  echo "== captured submission.patch (${_SUBSZ} bytes, $(grep -ac '^diff --git' "$_SUB" 2>/dev/null || echo 0) files) ==" \
    | tee -a "$STDOUT_LOG"
fi


# 1. Restore every path test.patch touches. Both diff headers are read, so new files, binary
#    baselines (image-comparison PNGs, snapshots), renames and deletions are all covered.
_patch_paths=$( { sed -n 's#^diff --git a/\(.*\) b/.*#\1#p' /tests/test.patch
                  sed -n 's#^diff --git a/.* b/\(.*\)#\1#p' /tests/test.patch; } | sort -u )
for _p in $_patch_paths; do
  git -C /app checkout harbor_base -- "$_p" 2>/dev/null || rm -rf "/app/$_p" 2>/dev/null || true
done
for _d in $PROTECTED_DIRS; do
  git -C /app checkout harbor_base -- "$_d" 2>/dev/null || true
  git -C /app clean -fdq -- "$_d" 2>/dev/null || true
done

# 2. Apply the hidden tests.
echo "== applying test.patch ==" | tee -a "$STDOUT_LOG"
git apply --binary /tests/test.patch 2>>"$STDERR_LOG" \
  || git apply /tests/test.patch 2>>"$STDERR_LOG" \
  || patch -p1 -i /tests/test.patch 2>>"$STDERR_LOG" \
  || { echo "ERROR: could not apply test.patch" | tee -a "$STDERR_LOG"; exit 1; }

# 3. Run only the configured tests.
python3 - <<'PY' > "$TEST_IDS_FILE"
import json
c = json.load(open("/tests/config.json"))
print("\n".join(c["f2p"] + c["p2p"]))

echo "== running f2p + p2p tests ==" | tee -a "$STDOUT_LOG"
( cd /app && run_tests ) >>"$STDOUT_LOG" 2>>"$STDERR_LOG" \
  || echo "(tests exited non-zero; parsing the report)" | tee -a "$STDOUT_LOG"

# 4. Reward from the report.
echo "== computing reward ==" | tee -a "$STDOUT_LOG"
# Rubric judge — SUB-AGENT backend: no API key, no network. On the first pass there is no
# verdict yet, so judge.py writes a judge request under /logs/verifier/judge/ and prints
# nothing; scoring falls back to tests alone. Once a judge sub-agent has written
# verdict.json there, `mm_run.sh <task> rescore` folds the verdict into the reward.
# The `|| echo ""` is load-bearing: the judge must never be able to fail the run.
RUBRIC=""
if [ -f /tests/rubrics.json ]; then
  RUBRIC=$(python3 /tests/judge.py --rubrics /tests/rubrics.json --repo /app \
             2>/logs/verifier/judge.log || echo "")
  echo "Rubric verdict: ${RUBRIC:-pending (judge request written; rescore after grading)}"
fi

python3 /tests/verifier.py "${REPORTS[@]}" --rubric "${RUBRIC:-}"

echo "reward=$(cat /logs/verifier/reward.txt 2>/dev/null)" | tee -a "$STDOUT_LOG"

def load_junit(path):
    """Every reported test, keyed by "classname name" and by name; a key seen twice with different
    outcomes counts as failed."""
    results = {}
    if not os.path.exists(path):
        return results
    try:
        root = ET.parse(path).getroot()
    except ET.ParseError:
        return results
    for tc in root.iter("testcase"):
        tags = {c.tag for c in tc}
        outcome = "skip" if "skipped" in tags else ("fail" if tags & {"failure", "error"} else "pass")
        full = f"{tc.get('classname', '')} {tc.get('name', '')}".strip()
        for key in {full, tc.get("name", "")}:
            if key in results and results[key] != outcome:
                results[key] = "fail"
            else:

    return results
